# AI contribution guidance: Shiny Waste Data

> This guidance applies only to `projects/shiny-waste-data/`. It does not define requirements for other repository projects, which have their own scope and maintainers.

This is a hackathon prototype: help people explore, ask questions, and try ideas. Prefer welcoming, understandable changes over unnecessary complexity; document what an experiment shows and what it does not show.

## Contributing to this project

- Work on a dedicated, descriptive branch and submit changes as a pull request for human review. Do not commit directly to the default branch or merge your own pull request.
- Keep changes focused. Explain the purpose, important trade-offs, and relevant verification in the pull request.
- Documentation is king: keep this project's README current, and document important behavior, data interpretation, assumptions, and steps needed to run or reproduce changes alongside the code.
- Keep project changes within this directory unless a requested change clearly requires repository-level work. Follow the existing R Shiny structure: `app.R`, `ui/`, and `R/`. `app.R` explicitly sources these files; preserve dependency order when adding or moving a helper.
- Ask the project maintainer when requirements or data interpretations are unclear; do not silently make consequential assumptions.

## Data and interpretation

- Record data sources, versions or dates, licensing, coverage, units, and transformations. Preserve source data and make derived data reproducible.
- Distinguish directly reported values from estimates. State assumptions, missingness, comparability limits, and other material caveats; do not present correlation as causation.
- In the Waste Transition view, material composition values are percentages of MSW. Applying a reported share to projected 2030 MSW generation produces an exploratory estimate, not a directly reported material projection; explain the assumption that composition remains representative.
- Avoid adding large files, credentials, or private information. Do not include deployment-generated changes unless necessary and explained.

## Code and verification

- Read the [project README](README.md) before changing behavior and preserve existing behavior outside the requested change.
- Treat reported observations, projections, interpolations, and scenario estimates as different things. Do not describe a visualization or association as causal evidence.
- Run relevant checks using the project's available setup. Report what passed, failed, or could not be run; do not claim checks that were not performed.
